scope: Numerical verification of the Level 8 Integrated Gradients engine against an independent exact oracle. It is NOT evidence of model validity, of real-world predictive value, or of production performance.

provenance.historical_f2b: Feasibility experiment F2B (scratch harness, not in this repository). Reported unchanged, for context only.
provenance.l8_1: Level 8 milestone L8-1: tests/test_level8_engine.py run against src/level8_explain.py in the canonical image.

straddle_threshold.selection: smallest abs(logit) from a development-range pool

grid_construction.api_corners: 32 corners of the Level 7 API bounds (digest only; not explained)
grid_construction.api_wide: 100 uniform API-bound points (digest only; not explained)

cross_check.provenance: HISTORICAL, MANUALLY RECORDED. Not produced by the test suite and not reproducible from this repository.
cross_check.what: A one-time comparison, made during L8-1, of the four digests above against grids built by the original external F2B scratch harness (which is not part of this repository). They were bit-identical.
cross_check.what_the_repository_can_check: The recorded digests are re-verified against the repository grid builder (tests/level8_oracle.py) by test_grid_digests_match_committed_evidence; that check does not involve the F2B harness.

acceptance_criteria.top_feature: engine top-1 within oracle set with abs >= max abs - 0.005

historical_f2b_results.label: HISTORICAL. Scratch harness, same configuration, 1 torch thread.
historical_f2b_results.determinism: Identical attributions across repeated calls, across 1/2/4/8 torch threads and 5 processes (F2).
historical_f2b_results.excluded: Gauss-Legendre timings and runs with invalid latency measurements are deliberately not reproduced here.

l8_1_results.label: CURRENT. Regenerated by the test suite against the corrected engine (L8-1 as amended by L8-1R).

l8_1r_corrections.label: Corrections made after the L8-1 pre-commit review. Numerical settings and tolerances are unchanged.
items: Oversized integers in continuous fields are rejected as invalid input instead of escaping as OverflowError.
explain_standardized is now the private _explain_standardized and returns finite floats only; the public result is built in explain() from validated input and serializes with allow_nan=False.
Probability is computed with a numerically stable sigmoid; non-finite logits fail closed.
The grid cross-check is recorded explicitly as a historical, manually recorded comparison.
accepted_limitations: numpy float32 scalars are rejected at the public Python interface.
Mirrored Level 7 prediction bounds are synchronized by a regex test over the service source.
The shared-engine concurrency collapse has no known root cause; serialized execution only mitigates it.
Image-layout (flat /app) overlay verification is deferred to integration.

historical_performance_reference.label: HISTORICAL, machine-specific, non-gating. Not a production claim.
historical_performance_reference.shared_engine_concurrency: Sharing one engine across concurrent callers collapsed to ~750 ms per call; root cause unexplained. Serialized execution was verified to avoid it.

l8_1_performance_smoke.includes: validation, ModelRuntime.preprocess, ModelRuntime.predict, IG (800 steps), residual check
l8_1_performance_smoke.conditions: canonical Linux/amd64 image; run with --cpus=1 when generating the committed evidence; 100 development-range inputs x2 after 30 warm-up calls; non-gating beyond the 25 ms p95 target

notices: Attributions describe how this frozen, development-only model's logit differs from its logit at baseline B0; they are not causal effects and do not show what would happen if a person changed a behaviour.
Baseline B0 is the training mean of every feature, including a fractional prior_injury of about 0.167. No real person has that value; it is a reference point, not a typical or healthy athlete.
Explanation eligibility is a development-range check. It does not establish statistical in-distribution status or real-world predictive validity.
Verification of the numbers (agreement with an independent oracle) is separate from model validity and from production performance.
